meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the play open, so of course it's cleaner. And you skipped my question: who decided, and was Owen heard first?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
You still haven't answered how that zero got entered without anyone calling me. And a version history I can't see is just a phrase, so turn the screen.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology, an explanation of who entered it and why no one called me first, and to see the version history you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, an answer on how the mark went in before anyone called her, and to see the version history; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, and the meeting ended well before her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her position, though your comparison with his dated in-class writing from September 24 was the kind of specific, checkable evidence that could have, had you answered her point that a timed piece and a weekend essay aren't comparable.
What cost ground: You passed over her question twice about who entered the zero and whether Owen was heard first, which kept her focused on procedure and made her distrust everything that followed.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since you mentioned a version history but never showed any times from it; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after her first question, admit in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put the version history on the screen instead of only naming it.
